evidence.snippet: Objective: To develop RESPClinBench, a real-world scenario-based benchmark for respiratory clinical decision-making, and evaluate seven contemporary large language models across AECOPD-PIM and PNBIM.

claire_radar.motivation: Background: Respiratory specialty care requires multimodal interpretation, longitudinal risk assessment, guideline-concordant intervention, and whole-course management, which are poorly represented by examination-oriented medical benchmarks.
claire_radar.name: RESPClinBench
claire_radar.oneLine: Evaluates clinical decision-making in respiratory specialty care using 623 multimodal cases, including AECOPD-PIM with 427 open-ended COPD cases and PNBIM with 196 pulmonary nodule cases that combine chest CT with clinical information.
claire_radar.paperTitle: RESPClinBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making and Longitudinal Disease Management in Respiratory Specialty Care

authors: Mouxiao Bian and Zhi Chen and Ruiyao Chen and Lu Lu and Hengrui Liang and Chaoyi Huang and Yiluo Lin and Jingru Ding and Yun Zhong and Yueming Su and Jie Xu
source.title: RESPClinBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making and Longitudinal Disease Management in Respiratory Specialty Care

claire_radar.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in examination-oriented medical benchmarks by testing long-horizon disease management and multimodal interpretation in respiratory care.
